nodes.description: Public contract state variable 'uint entropy' that stores the accumulated entropy and is both read and rewritten inside getRandomNumber().
Public function getRandomNumber() that derives a 'random' number purely from on-chain block data and returns the mutated state variable entropy.

Block-level miner/validator controlled input (block context: blockhash, block.number, block.timestamp) used as the only entropy source of the contract, making the result predictable and manipulable by block producers.

Unsafe operation 'entropy ^= uint(blockhash(entropy % block.number))' which mixes miner-influenceable block data (blockhash / block.number, i.e. block context) into the state variable, producing deterministic, publicly computable pseudo-randomness, and returns the state directly.

edges.reason: Miner/validator controlled block context (blockhash(entropy % block.number), block.number/timestamp domain) is the sole entropy feed into the entropy update, so the returned 'random' value depends on manipulable block-level input.
State variable entropy is read as the left operand of the XOR and as the index seed of the modulo, flowing into the entropy update computation.
The block-data-derived value is written back into the state variable entropy, permanently poisoning the contract's entropy source with cheaply predictable information.
Execution of getRandomNumber() always reaches the state-mutating entropy ^= uint(blockhash(...)) operation before returning.
The updated entropy value computed by the unsafe operation is returned by getRandomNumber() as the 'random number'.
